blind_rationale:
Jiang and Zheng (2014) assemble a 10-year utility-city panel (1998-2007) of 208 large and medium urban water utilities across 192 prefecture-level Chinese cities to evaluate the causal impact of private sector participation (PSP: any nonstate equity capital share, and disaggregated into PSP majority with >50% nonstate capital vs PSP minority with >0% to <50% nonstate capital, compared against 100% state-owned utilities).

1. Narrow Criterion 2 (Rule/Ownership Mechanism): Satisfied (`yes_rule_mechanism`). The exposure captures municipal water utility ownership privatization (share transfers and joint ventures enabled by China's 2001 State Planning Committee guidelines and 2002/2004 Ministry of Construction marketization and concession decrees, MOC Circular No. 272 and Decree No. 126). One caveat is that PSP is operationalized via corporate balance-sheet capital shares (`state capital share < 1` or `<= 50%`), so non-equity public-private contracts (BOT/TOT) remain coded in the state-owned reference group, and specific tariff or connection rules are not directly observed.

2. Criterion 4 (Water/Sanitation Service Access Outcome) & Sign Interpretation: While the bulk of the paper (Tables 5-7, 12 indicators) evaluates corporate financial, employment, and productivity metrics that do not measure household service access (and would fail Criterion 4 under E04 if extracted alone), Section V.D (Table 8, PDF p. 30 / journal p. 184) explicitly tests three city/utility water service outcomes merged from the China City Statistical Yearbooks:
   - `Domestic water supply population (log)` (N = 814 utility-years), defined in Table A1 (PDF p. 32) as the number of urban domestic water users (imputed from total urban domestic water supply divided by per capita domestic water use). Because the two-way fixed-effects specification controls for `Population` (log total city population), positive coefficients represent an expansion in the urban domestic water service population/coverage (`PSP` original beta = +0.026, SE = 0.025, ns; `PSP` corrective recoding beta = +0.037, SE = 0.026, ns; `PSP majority` original beta = +0.032, SE = 0.026, ns; `PSP majority` corrective recoding beta = +0.046*, SE = 0.026, p < 0.10). This satisfies Criterion 4 (`yes_household_or_service_access`), albeit as an aggregate city-level imputed user count that the authors themselves describe as suggestive/conjectural.
   - By contrast, `Urban water supply (log)` (N = 1,752; `PSP` beta = -0.020 to -0.038) and `Urban domestic water supply (log)` (N = 814; `PSP` beta = -0.054 to -0.044; `PSP majority` original beta = -0.071*, SE = 0.038) measure aggregate water volume supplied. Their negative raw signs DO NOT clearly indicate reduced household access because, as the authors emphasize (PDF p. 27), decreased water production/supply volume alongside increased domestic users plausibly reflects reduced pipeline water leakage rather than lower user consumption.

3. Blind SWiM Family Placement: `Family C` (ownership, regulation, institutional capacity, administrative structure). Substantively, testing private vs state utility ownership (`PSP` / `PSP majority`) on domestic water service population (`Domestic water supply population (log)`, Table 8) maps directly to Family C's utility ownership/privatization domain. A `none_nonfit` classification would only be warranted if (a) Family C strictly excludes aggregate city-level imputed log user counts in favor of direct household-level connection rates, or (b) the prior extraction erroneously pulled a corporate financial metric from Tables 5-7 or an aggregate water volume metric (`Urban water supply (log)` / `Urban domestic water supply (log)`) whose direction with respect to household access is confounded by leakage reduction.

headline_estimate_summary:
1) Water Service & Coverage Outcomes (Table 8, PDF p. 30 / p. 184; two-way utility and year FE linear panel models controlling for 1-year lagged utility variables and 1-year lagged city variables including log city population, utility-clustered SEs, reference = 100% state-owned utilities):
- Domestic water supply population (log number of urban domestic water users, N = 814): PSP (original coding) beta = +0.026 (SE = 0.025, p >= 0.10, R2 = 0.247); PSP (corrective recoding) beta = +0.037 (SE = 0.026, p >= 0.10, R2 = 0.248); PSP majority (original) beta = +0.032 (SE = 0.026, p >= 0.10) & PSP minority (original) beta = +0.006 (SE = 0.034, p >= 0.10, R2 = 0.248); PSP majority (corrective recoding) beta = +0.046* (SE = 0.026, p < 0.10, ~4.6% increase in domestic water users) & PSP minority (corrective recoding) beta = +0.015 (SE = 0.038, p >= 0.10, R2 = 0.250).
- Urban domestic water supply volume (log, N = 814): PSP (original) beta = -0.054 (SE = 0.044, ns); PSP (recoded) beta = -0.044 (SE = 0.052, ns); PSP majority (original) beta = -0.071* (SE = 0.038, p < 0.10) & PSP minority beta = -0.003 (SE = 0.082, ns); PSP majority (recoded) beta = -0.062 (SE = 0.047, ns) & PSP minority beta = +0.003 (SE = 0.088, ns).
- Total urban water supply volume (log, N = 1,752): PSP (original) beta = -0.020 (SE = 0.026, ns); PSP (recoded) beta = -0.038 (SE = 0.030, ns); PSP majority (original) beta = -0.040 (SE = 0.030, ns) & PSP minority beta = +0.017 (SE = 0.040, ns); PSP majority (recoded) beta = -0.055 (SE = 0.035, ns) & PSP minority beta = -0.008 (SE = 0.043, ns).

2) Primary Utility Financial/Operational Performance Outcomes (Tables 5-7, PDF pp. 22-29; two-way FE or Arellano-Bond dynamic panel models with full utility and city controls):
- General PSP (Table 5 Col 3, original coding): Employment (log) beta = -0.0918** (SE = 0.0404, p < 0.05, N = 1,547); Managerial expense-to-sales ratio beta = -0.0274* (SE = 0.0145, p < 0.10, N = 1,752); Profit-to-sales ratio beta = +0.0150 (SE = 0.0205, ns, N = 1,515; in corrective recoding Table 6 Col 6, beta = +0.0550**, SE = 0.0253, p < 0.05, N = 1,515); Investment beta = +10,568 (SE = 19,987, ns, N = 1,752); TFP (log) beta = +0.209 (SE = 0.389, ns, N = 1,507).
- Authors' preferred disaggregated specification (Table 7 Col 6, PDF pp. 28-29, corrective recoding, full controls): PSP majority on Employment (log) beta = -0.119*** (SE = 0.0399, p < 0.01, N = 1,547), on Managerial expense ratio beta = -0.0212* (SE = 0.0127, p < 0.10, N = 1,752), and on Profit-sales ratio beta = +0.0714** (SE = 0.0336, p < 0.05, N = 1,515); corresponding PSP minority estimates are statistically insignificant.
study_design_and_sample: Longitudinal utility-city panel study (two-way utility and year fixed-effects linear panel models and Arellano-Bond dynamic panel models) in China over 1998-2007, merging the National Bureau of Statistics Annual Industrial Firm Surveys (industry code 4610) with China City Statistical Yearbooks (1999-2008). Unit of analysis: large and medium-sized urban water utilities in prefecture-level cities (208 urban water utilities across 192 cities). Analytic sample sizes: N = 814 utility-year observations for city domestic water supply volume and domestic water supply population (Table 8); N = 1,752 utility-years for total urban water supply (Table 8); and N = 1,507 to 2,072 utility-years across the 12 firm-level financial/efficiency outcomes (Tables 5-7).
